provenance.note: This proposal has not been validated against the Stage 0 gold set and must not be used as an authoritative Q-matrix or learner model.

mathematical_content.description: The mathematical idea or relation that must be understood, independent of the solution strategy or presentation.

reasoning_move.description: A general-purpose inference or problem-solving move that can transfer across mathematical topics.

procedure.description: An explicit, teachable sequence of actions that produces or organizes part of a solution.

representation.description: How the item presents information. Use for controlled contrasts and retrieval, not as proof of a mathematical weakness.

cognitive_demand.description: How directly or flexibly the item asks the learner to use reviewed skills.

nuisance_load.description: Incidental demand that can affect performance without being the mathematical target.

prerequisite.semantics: from_skill_id should be sufficiently established before instruction on to_skill_id.

part_of.semantics: from_skill_id is a narrower component or procedure within to_skill_id.

often_combined_with.semantics: The skills frequently occur in the same reviewed solution path but remain distinct.

contrasts_with.semantics: The skills have a boundary that reviewers and annotators should explicitly distinguish.

alternative_to.semantics: The skills may support different legitimate paths to the same result.

curriculum_gating.note: Every relation in this proposal is unreviewed, so none may gate curriculum.

representation.name: Story text
representation.description: Quantities and relations are embedded in prose.

representation.name: Symbolic expression
representation.description: The main information is given with numerals or mathematical symbols.

representation.name: Table
representation.description: Rows and columns organize the relevant information.

representation.name: Number line
representation.description: Order, distance, or operations are shown on a line.

representation.name: Grid
representation.description: Cells, lattice points, or coordinates carry essential information.

representation.name: Clock or calendar
representation.description: Time is presented on a clock face, schedule, or calendar.

representation.name: Two-dimensional geometric diagram
representation.description: A planar diagram is essential to interpreting the item.

representation.name: Three-dimensional solid diagram
representation.description: A drawing or net represents a three-dimensional object.

representation.name: Spatial transformation
representation.description: Before-and-after views or movement cues encode a spatial change.

representation.name: Graph or network
representation.description: Nodes and connections encode routes or relationships.

representation.name: Physical arrangement
representation.description: Objects, people, tokens, or containers are arranged visually.

representation.name: Mixed representation
representation.description: Two or more representations are jointly essential.

skills.name: Counting and cardinality
skills.description: Count a finite set once each and understand that the final count names its quantity.
skills.boundary_note: Does not include organizing a complex case space; use systematic enumeration for that reasoning move.

skills.name: Place value
skills.description: Interpret, compose, decompose, and compare whole numbers by the value of each digit position.
skills.boundary_note: Digit-pattern observations belong to numeric patterns unless positional value is required.

skills.name: Whole-number addition and subtraction
skills.description: Model and calculate combining, separating, and additive comparison with whole numbers.
skills.boundary_note: Regrouping is a procedure; choosing addition or subtraction from constraints is a reasoning decision.

skills.name: Whole-number multiplication and division
skills.description: Model and calculate equal groups, multiplicative comparison, sharing, and grouping with whole numbers.
skills.boundary_note: Equal-groups arrays are a procedure and representation of this content skill.

skills.name: Arithmetic expressions
skills.description: Interpret and evaluate grouped or multi-operation arithmetic expressions in the intended order.
skills.boundary_note: Simple single-operation calculation should use the corresponding operation skill instead.

skills.name: Fractions as parts and quantities
skills.description: Interpret a fraction as equal parts of a whole, a set, or a quantity.
skills.boundary_note: Comparing or renaming fractions belongs to fraction equivalence and comparison.

skills.name: Fraction equivalence and comparison
skills.description: Recognize equivalent fractions and order fractions using common references or structure.
skills.boundary_note: The common-reference algorithm is modeled separately as a procedure.

skills.name: Ratio and proportional reasoning
skills.description: Reason about equivalent multiplicative relationships between two quantities.
skills.boundary_note: Equal sharing alone is division; a ratio requires relating two varying quantities.

skills.name: Factors and multiples
skills.description: Identify factor pairs, common factors, multiples, and common multiples of whole numbers.
skills.boundary_note: Fast rule-based divisibility judgments are tracked separately from the factor relation itself.

skills.name: Divisibility reasoning
skills.description: Determine whether a whole number is divisible by another using structure or divisibility rules.
skills.boundary_note: A remainder or repeating-state question belongs to remainders and cycles when divisibility is not the target.

skills.name: Remainders and cycles
skills.description: Reason about leftover quantities and repeating states indexed by a whole-number cycle.
skills.boundary_note: Merely recognizing a visual repetition belongs to numeric or visual pattern reasoning.

skills.name: Even and odd structure
skills.description: Classify quantities by parity and reason about how operations preserve or change evenness.
skills.boundary_note: Parity is the mathematical content; invariant reasoning is the transferable move when parity is used to prove impossibility.

skills.name: Numeric patterns and sequences
skills.description: Identify, continue, or describe a rule relating ordered numbers or repeated numeric states.
skills.boundary_note: Inferring a transferable rule is pattern generalization; the number relation itself is this content skill.

skills.name: Unknowns and equations
skills.description: Represent and solve equality relationships containing one or more unknown quantities.
skills.boundary_note: A missing number found by counting alone should not be labeled as equation solving.

skills.name: Inequalities and bounds
skills.description: Interpret and constrain a quantity using greater-than, less-than, minimum, maximum, or interval relations.
skills.boundary_note: Estimating a useful bound is a reasoning move; interpreting the bound relation is this content skill.

skills.name: Length and distance
skills.description: Measure, compare, add, or infer one-dimensional lengths and distances.
skills.boundary_note: Converting length units is a procedure; tracing a boundary total is perimeter.

skills.name: Perimeter
skills.description: Reason about the total boundary length of a two-dimensional figure.
skills.boundary_note: Do not infer perimeter mastery from area questions or vice versa.

skills.name: Area
skills.description: Reason about two-dimensional measure using unit squares, decomposition, or known area relations.
skills.boundary_note: Counting visible objects is cardinality unless equal area units are essential.

skills.name: Clock and calendar structure
skills.description: Interpret clock faces, schedules, day cycles, weeks, months, and calendar relationships.
skills.boundary_note: Computing a duration step by step is the elapsed-time procedure.

skills.name: Money and value
skills.description: Compose, compare, and exchange monetary amounts in a stated currency system.
skills.boundary_note: Generic proportional price comparison may also require ratio reasoning; do not merge the two skills.

skills.name: Measurement units
skills.description: Understand what standard units measure and the multiplicative relationships among compatible units.
skills.boundary_note: Executing a conversion is a procedure; recognizing the unit relationship is this content skill.

skills.name: Angles and turns
skills.description: Interpret and compare corners, directions, and full or partial turns.
skills.boundary_note: Tracking a whole figure through a turn belongs to geometric transformations as well.

skills.name: Two-dimensional shape properties
skills.description: Identify and reason from sides, vertices, angles, containment, and adjacency in planar figures.
skills.boundary_note: Rearranging pieces into a target uses spatial composition; movement of a shape uses transformations.

skills.name: Three-dimensional solid properties
skills.description: Reason about faces, edges, vertices, visibility, nets, and assembly of solid objects.
skills.boundary_note: A diagram of a solid is a representation tag; the structural relationships are this skill.

skills.name: Symmetry and reflection structure
skills.description: Recognize or construct correspondence across a line or around a center of symmetry.
skills.boundary_note: Using symmetry to reduce cases is symmetry exploitation, a reasoning move; carrying out a reflection is also a transformation.

skills.name: Geometric transformations
skills.description: Track position, orientation, and preserved features under translation, rotation, or reflection.
skills.boundary_note: A static symmetry property is not by itself evidence of tracking a transformation.

skills.name: Spatial composition and dissection
skills.description: Compose, partition, fold, unfold, or rearrange parts while preserving their spatial relationships.
skills.boundary_note: Area may be supporting content, but visual assembly without measure remains a distinct skill.

skills.name: Grid and coordinate location
skills.description: Locate and relate positions using rows, columns, ordered moves, or coordinate pairs.
skills.boundary_note: Counting all possible routes across a grid is the grid-path procedure and often combinatorial content.

skills.name: Combinatorial counting
skills.description: Count distinct arrangements, selections, or routes without omission or double counting.
skills.boundary_note: Systematic enumeration is a reasoning move and tables or trees are procedures used to establish the count.

skills.name: Elementary probability
skills.description: Compare or calculate likelihood from equally likely outcomes in a finite sample space.
skills.boundary_note: Building the sample space may require combinatorial counting, but likelihood is the distinct target here.

skills.name: Systematic enumeration
skills.description: Generate possibilities in an organized order that supports checking completeness and uniqueness.
skills.boundary_note: The resulting number of cases is combinatorial content; the disciplined generation method is this reasoning move.

skills.name: Case analysis
skills.description: Partition a problem into exhaustive, non-overlapping conditions and resolve each condition.
skills.boundary_note: Listing unstructured examples is not sufficient evidence of case analysis.

skills.name: Working backward
skills.description: Start from a required final state and reverse valid steps to recover earlier states or choices.
skills.boundary_note: Applying an inverse operation once is not enough unless the solution is organized from the goal backward.

skills.name: Constraint propagation
skills.description: Use one restriction to narrow possibilities elsewhere, repeating until the configuration is determined.
skills.boundary_note: Reading a single inequality is content; propagating its consequences through linked choices is this move.

skills.name: Invariant reasoning
skills.description: Identify a property that remains unchanged or follows a fixed cycle across allowed operations.
skills.boundary_note: Parity is one possible invariant but should remain separately tagged as mathematical content when required.

skills.name: Decomposition and recomposition
skills.description: Break a quantity or structure into useful parts and recombine those parts to simplify the problem.
skills.boundary_note: A memorized regrouping algorithm is a procedure; choosing a useful decomposition is this reasoning move.

skills.name: Symmetry exploitation
skills.description: Use repeated or mirrored structure to reduce work, pair cases, or infer an unseen relation.
skills.boundary_note: Recognizing a symmetric figure alone is the symmetry content skill, not necessarily this strategy.

skills.name: Estimation and bounding
skills.description: Use a justified approximation, lower bound, or upper bound to rule out or select possibilities.
skills.boundary_note: A guess without a defensible bound is not evidence for this skill.

skills.name: Pattern generalization
skills.description: Infer a rule from examples and apply it beyond the immediately shown cases.
skills.boundary_note: Continuing a familiar count by rote does not establish generalization.

skills.name: Elimination of impossible choices
skills.description: Reject candidates by a necessary condition without fully constructing every remaining solution.
skills.boundary_note: Selecting an answer because it looks plausible is not elimination; a stated constraint must rule choices out.

skills.name: Counterexample testing
skills.description: Test a claim or candidate by constructing a valid case that would make it fail.
skills.boundary_note: A failed random trial is not sufficient unless it logically refutes the relevant universal claim.

skills.name: Translation between representations
skills.description: Preserve the same mathematical relationships while moving between words, symbols, diagrams, tables, or models.
skills.boundary_note: A representation tag records what the item shows; this skill requires the learner to connect two forms.

skills.name: Regrouping whole numbers
skills.description: Exchange equivalent place-value units while adding or subtracting whole numbers.
skills.boundary_note: This is the explicit exchange procedure, not all whole-number addition and subtraction.

skills.name: Equal-groups and array modeling
skills.description: Construct equal groups or rectangular arrays to represent multiplication and division.
skills.boundary_note: Fluent multiplication calculation may occur without constructing this model.

skills.name: Common-reference fraction comparison
skills.description: Rename or align fractions to a common denominator, numerator, benchmark, or diagram for comparison.
skills.boundary_note: Conceptual recognition of equivalence is content; this is an explicit comparison procedure.

skills.name: Organize cases in a table
skills.description: Record cases in rows and columns chosen to expose coverage, constraints, or repeated structure.
skills.boundary_note: Reading a provided table is a representation demand; constructing one deliberately is this procedure.

skills.name: Enumerate with a tree diagram
skills.description: Branch choices by stage so every outcome appears once along a root-to-leaf path.
skills.boundary_note: A decorative branching picture is not evidence; the branches must encode an exhaustive staged choice.

skills.name: Count constrained grid paths
skills.description: Count routes on a grid while respecting allowed directions, barriers, or required points.
skills.boundary_note: Following one path tests location or movement; counting the full valid route set is this procedure.

skills.name: Correct overlap with inclusion-exclusion
skills.description: Combine counts while explicitly subtracting or restoring cases counted in multiple groups.
skills.boundary_note: Simple disjoint addition is not inclusion-exclusion because no overlap correction is required.

skills.name: Calculate elapsed time
skills.description: Move between start, duration, and end time across clock or calendar boundaries.
skills.boundary_note: Reading a clock value alone is time content, not this multi-state procedure.

skills.name: Convert compatible measurement units
skills.description: Multiply or divide by a known unit relationship while preserving the measured quantity.
skills.boundary_note: Choosing an appropriate unit is measurement content; executing the conversion is this procedure.

skills.name: Add a useful partition or auxiliary mark
skills.description: Introduce a line, region, label, or mark that reveals hidden geometric or counting structure.
skills.boundary_note: The added mark must support a valid solution step; arbitrary drawing is not this procedure.
